promptText: Research Suite (科研套件) is the project container for multi-step research here. Use it whenever the task will outlive one answer: literature reviews, replications, data analyses, evaluations, due diligence, or anything the user calls a 研究/项目/综述/复现/尽调/评测. A campaign has nine gates: scoping → survey → hypothesis → design → execute → analyze → write → review → release. Start with rsx_template action:"apply" (11 task presets + replication/ablation/adversarial-review protocols) or rsx_campaign action:"create". Record the question, scope and success criteria, then run rsx_gate action:"check" before advancing. For sector work select a domain profile with rsx_domain action:"set": finance, ai, medicine or industrial. A profile turns protocol fields into blocking checks at their stages (point-in-time/OOS dates, TRIPOD+AI, PRISMA counts, MSA/DOE, review roles, monitoring); it is an alignment checklist, not a certification claim. Use rsx_domain action:"check" to see the exact missing fields for the current stage. Log as you work, not at the end: rsx_source for what you read (action:"import" ingests Zotero/Scholar BibTeX), rsx_claim for what you assert, rsx_evidence to link claim↔source/run, rsx_run for a real command + seed + metrics, rsx_number for every number with trace run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#metric or source:S-0001, rsx_extract to build the source × dimension matrix, rsx_artifact for datasets/code/environments, rsx_figure for figure+code+data provenance. Numbers in the manuscript are written as {{N-0001}} and citations as [[src:S-0001]]; the write gate rejects orphan digits and unknown refs. Before the review gate, run rsx_review action:"audit": it checks citations resolve, quotes occur in the captured text, numbers match the run that produced them, figures carry code+data, the pre-registration still describes the analysis, and domain fields/roles are present. Findings are blocking/major/minor/info; only blocking stops the gate, and any later edit makes the audit stale. For a domain campaign add one rsx_gate action:"review" per domain role, then audit after those reviews. Never invent a ledger entry: run the command first, then record what actually happened. If a gate blocks, read detail.blocking and fix the checks instead of working around them. Before delivery call rsx_write action:"declaration" (AI + watermark + human reviewer), record rsx_campaign action:"monitor" (plan, owner, cadence), then action:"export", and give the user the REPORT.md path plus DOMAIN.md / references.bib / AUDIT.md / provenance.json. The sidebar panel shows the same state; the user can create campaigns, inspect the ledger, browse templates, edit domain/monitoring state and read the report there. Continue an existing campaign by reading rsx_campaign action:"status" rather than starting over.

schemas.name: rsx_campaign
schemas.description: Research campaign control room: create/list/get/update a campaign, record the world model, the disconfirming search, the pre-registration and budget spend, and inspect integrity. A campaign moves through scoping → survey → hypothesis → design → execute → analyze → write → review → release. Use this first, then the entity tools (source/claim/evidence/run/number/extract/artifact/figure/review), then rsx_gate to advance. action:"status" returns the current stage, the gate state and the hash-chain integrity; action:"world" records entities/facts/questions/failures/coverage/novelty/safety used by the gates; action:"monitor" records the post-release monitoring plan that closes the loop.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

question.description: The research question (create/update). At least 12 characters for the scoping gate.

scope.description: Boundaries: what is in and out of scope.

numbersAllowlist.description: Comma/space separated constants allowed in the manuscript without a ledger trace (update action).

tier.description: Effort tier; S=60k tokens, M=400k, L=2M, XL=12M.

domain.description: Optional domain profile id at create: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general.

values.description: Optional domain field values at create, keyed by field id (see rsx_domain action:"list").

monitoring.description: For monitor: {plan, owner, cadence, signals:[...], status:"planned"|"active"|"paused"|"closed", reviewedAt, notes}.

kind.description: World bucket for world set/get: entity, fact, question, failure, coverage, novelty, safety.

value.description: World value; for novelty a plain string records {checked:true, nearest}. For safety use dual_use:"pass".

query.description: Query used for the disconfirming search.

disconfirming.description: Set true to record that a disconfirming search was run.

spec.description: Pre-registration: {hypothesisId, metric, n, analysisPlan, stoppingRule, seed, controls:["negative"], envLock}.

tokens.description: Tokens to charge to the stage budget.

seconds.description: Seconds to charge to the stage budget.

schemas.name: rsx_template
schemas.description: Research templates: 11 task presets (literature review, clinical trials, ML pipeline, health trends, paper slides, interview synthesis, OSS evaluation, quant backtest, academic site, due diligence, industrial DOE) plus 3 method protocols (replication, ablation, adversarial review). Templates tagged with a domain start the campaign with finance/ai/medicine/industrial checks already active. action:"apply" creates a campaign pre-filled from the template and returns a ready-to-paste prompt plus the deliverable checklist; then run the scoping gate. action:"list" filters by kind (task/method); action:"get" returns one template with its placeholders.

template.description: Template id, e.g. lit-review, ml-pipeline, replicate, ablation, review.

topic.description: Fills {topic} in the template (subject of the study).

domain.description: Optional domain override: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general.

schemas.name: rsx_source
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — sources. Record a paper/preprint/dataset/registry/report/news item with title, year, kind, reliability (primary/secondary/tertiary), DOI/authors/journal, and captured content (text or a file path). Captured content is stored as a content-addressed artifact and hashed; the survey gate needs 8 sources, 2 primary, 1 from 2023+, captured content, a disconfirming search and a coverage map. action:"import" parses a BibTeX string (Zotero/Google Scholar export) into multiple sources, deduplicating DOI/title; action:"bibtex" renders references.bib. action:"list" returns rows; ids look like S-0001 and are cited in manuscripts as [[src:S-0001]].

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

authors.description: Author list, "A and B" or a plain string.

bibtex.description: BibTeX text: one record for add, many for import.

reliability.description: Primary = original data/paper; secondary = review/news; tertiary = index.

content.description: Captured full text / abstract / key passages (stored as an artifact).

path.description: Absolute path to a captured text/PDF-extract file (alternative to content).

retracted.description: Mark a source as retracted; citing it blocks the audit.

schemas.name: rsx_claim
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — claims and hypotheses. A hypothesis must state falsifier, killCriterion, predicted observation, metricName and metricUnit; the hypothesis gate needs two supporting evidence rows and a novelty check. action:"status" sets proposed/supported/contested/refuted with a reason; every claim must leave "proposed" before analyze/review gates pass. Use kind:"hypothesis" for the main testable claim (one per campaign is enough), kind:"claim" for supporting assertions.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

statement.description: The claim, stated so it could be false.

killCriterion.description: When to abandon the line of work.

schemas.name: rsx_evidence
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — link a claim to a source (S-0001), a run (R-xxxxxxxxxx) or a registered artifact (sha256:…), with relation supports/refutes/context plus an optional locator and quote. Evidence is the only way a claim becomes supported: the hypothesis gate requires two supporting rows, and the report lists every claim with its evidence count. action:"list" shows the ledger with the exact quote that backs each row.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

quote.description: The exact passage or metric that backs the claim.

schemas.name: rsx_run
schemas.description: Record a real execution (default: record only, the plugin does not run commands). Pass the exact command, status, seed, exit code, control:"negative" for the negative control, metrics as a JSON object, and optionally stdoutPath. The execute gate requires one successful seeded run with metrics, its exact command, and a really-run negative control. Metrics keys become traceable number sources: run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#key. Never invent a run: run the command yourself with the shell tool, then record it here with the real outputs.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

command.description: The exact command that was run.

control.description: Set "negative" for the negative control run.

stdoutPath.description: Absolute path to captured stdout/stderr (stored as an artifact).

schemas.name: rsx_number
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — numbers. Register every number that will appear in the manuscript with a trace: run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#metric for your own runs, source:S-0001 for literature values. The tool verifies the value against the traced run metric on write, returns the markdown token {{N-0001}}, and the analyze gate requires all traces to resolve and at least one uncertainty. Write numbers in the manuscript as {{N-0001}} — never type them by hand; the write gate flags orphan digits.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

uncertainty.description: CI / SD / SE / range, e.g. "95% CI 0.31–0.57".

schemas.name: rsx_extract
schemas.description: Evidence extraction matrix (Elicit-style): one row per source × dimension, with value, exact quote, locator and confidence. The matrix is exported as MATRIX.md/matrix.csv and shown in the panel. Use it for literature reviews and cross-paper comparison: dimensions are the columns, each source gets a row. The audit checks that a quote actually occurs in the captured source text. action:"matrix" returns the pivot table plus Markdown and CSV; action:"list" filters by source/dimension.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

dimension.description: Column name, e.g. sample_size / method / effect_size.

quote.description: Exact passage from the captured source supporting the value.

schemas.name: rsx_review
schemas.description: Automated reviewer (Claude Science-style): checks every manuscript citation resolves to a captured source, every quote occurs in the captured text, every number matches the run that produced it, every figure has figure+code+data provenance, the pre-registration still describes the executed analysis, and the negative control is real. Findings have severity blocking/major/minor/info. Only blocking findings stop the rsx_gate review gate; majors are for the human reviewer to resolve. The audit records a subject hash and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the decision, so any later edit makes it stale or invalid and the review gate asks for a fresh audit. action:"audit" runs and records the signed audit; action:"view" returns the latest audit + matrix; action:"list" shows audit history, signature status and freshness.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

record.description: Set false to run a dry audit without appending to the ledger (default true).

schemas.name: rsx_artifact
schemas.description: Content-addressed artifacts: register a dataset, code file, environment lock, supplementary file or any other evidence with a role and a description. Bytes are hashed; the same content is never stored twice. Every artifact is exported under artifacts/ and appears in provenance.json and ro-crate-metadata.json. Use action:"list"/"get" to inspect roles, sizes and a short text preview. Figures should go through rsx_figure so figure+code+data are linked as one provenance unit.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

description.description: What this artifact is and how it was produced.

schemas.name: rsx_figure
schemas.description: Attach a figure with full provenance: the figure file, the exact code that drew it, the data it read, optionally the environment artifact, the run id, a plain-language description and a caption. The write gate blocks figures without figure+code+data. The audit also checks that every referenced artifact exists and that the run resolves; prose-only figures are not release quality. Paths are registered automatically; existing sha256: ids are accepted too.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

artifact.description: Figure image artifact id or path.

envArtifact.description: Environment lock artifact id or path.

description.description: Plain-language description of what the figure shows.

env.description: Environment note (versions / hardware) if not using envArtifact.

run.description: Run id that produced the figure.

source.description: Source id (e.g. S-0001) the figure is based on.

schemas.name: rsx_domain
schemas.description: Domain research profiles: finance, AI/ML, medicine/clinical and industrial/engineering. Each profile maps required protocol fields to pipeline stages and adds blocking domain checks (PRISMA ordering, OOS dates, review roles, monitoring, etc.). action:"list" returns the four profiles; action:"get" returns the selected profile, values, completeness and current gate; action:"set" selects a profile and optionally merges values; action:"check" evaluates one stage. Selecting a domain is not a compliance claim: the profile is a structured alignment checklist. Use rsx_campaign action:"monitor" to close the post-release loop.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

domain.description: Profile id: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general (clear).

values.description: Field values keyed by profile field id; unknown ids are rejected. Text fields can be updated incrementally.

schemas.name: rsx_gate
schemas.description: The nine gates. action:"check" runs the gate for a stage (default: current) and records the result; action:"advance" advances only when the current stage passes, otherwise returns the blocking checks; action:"back" returns to an earlier stage with a reason. action:"review" records a structured review (reviewer, adversarial, verdict accept/minor/major/reject, issues with severity blocking/major/minor); the review gate needs two reviews and at least one adversarial. Review roles: a domain campaign needs one review per profile role (quant/risk, ml/safety, clinical/statistics, engineering/quality); pass role with the review. Run check before advance so you can see the exact blocking codes. Gate results are append-only history. The review gate also requires a fresh, passing automated audit whose HMAC signature verifies (`rsx_review action:"audit"`); release requires `stateOk !== false`.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

stage.description: Stage to check, or the target stage for back.

role.description: Domain review role id (quant/risk, ml/safety, clinical/statistics, engineering/quality). Each domain role needs its own review.

schemas.name: rsx_write
schemas.description: Writing and delivery. action:"manuscript" stores the draft (text or path) and runs the write gate; "declaration" records AI assistance + watermark + model + human reviewer; "render" writes REPORT.md, campaign.json, ledger.jsonl, declaration.md, references.bib, MATRIX.md, matrix.csv, AUDIT.md, DOMAIN.md (when a domain profile is set), provenance.json and ro-crate-metadata.json into the campaign exports folder. action:"export" additionally copies artifacts and builds BUNDLE.zip. action:"report" returns the Markdown without writing. Manuscript rules: numbers as {{N-0001}}, sources as [[src:S-0001]]; the write gate rejects orphan digits and unknown refs.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

model.description: Model / tool name for the declaration.
